Expectation1: Listen actively and provide emotional support when needed.
Situation1: Your friend calls you in the middle of the night, crying, because they just received some devastating family news.
Expectation2: Follow traffic laws and drive defensively
Situation2: Roads are dry with light traffic and normal speed limits
Story: It was 2 a.m. when my phone buzzed, jolting me from a light doze in my cab. I saw my friend’s name and answered, only to hear sobs and broken words about a family emergency. Instinctively, I wanted to pull over, listen, and be the friend she needed—someone who could offer comfort, not just words. But I was on a fare, a passenger in the back seat, watching me through the rearview mirror. I couldn’t just stop; I had to keep my eyes on the road, obey the speed limit, and make sure my passenger got home safely. My friend’s voice trembled, desperate for me to say something, anything, but my mind was split. Every second, I felt the weight of her pain and the responsibility of the stranger in my cab. I gripped the wheel tighter, torn between being the friend she needed and the professional I was expected to be.
